item.title: Jalen Carter, Riq Woolen decline to speak to reporters after loss to Cowboys
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With all the focus on the injury issues for the Eagles' offense, the team's defense got manhandled last night by the Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
With all the focus on the injury issues for the Eagles' offense, the team's defense got manhandled last night by the Cowboys. After the game, two key players declined to speak to reporters.

Both defensive tackle Jalen Carter and cornerback Riq Woolen passed on the league-imposed requirement to talk after each game.

Said Carter, via EJ Smith of PHLY Sports, “Nah, y’all have a good night. You get home safe.”

Said Woolen, also per Smith, "Appreciate you all, as always. Y’all have a good night, get home safely as well."

It's not uncommon for players to refuse to speak after games. Sometimes, it morphs into a confrontation with the league, which has fined players in the past. More often than not, it gets resolved with a conversation or a warning.

The reluctance to speak is not surprising. The Eagles gave up 204 rushing yards to the Cowboys. Woolen slipped and fell on what would have been a long touchdown catch by receiver CeeDee Lamb, if the throw had been more accurate.

Beyond that, the Eagles are 2-5. The season is slipping away. Frustrations may have emerged, if either or both had spoken.

Still, the league mandates it. Last night, they both failed to satisfy the obligation.

item.title: Bill Belichick wants ACC to add more goal line cameras after controversial Syracuse finish
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: During much of his time in the NFL, Bill Belichick called for the NFL to spend the money necessary to install cameras that would make it easier to review plays.
item.content:encoded:
During much of his time in the NFL, Bill Belichick called for the NFL to spend the money necessary to install cameras that would make it easier to review plays. In his second season as a college coach, Belichick is banging that same drum.

Via Brian Murphy of WRAL, Belichick wants the ACC to add cameras at the goal line and along the sidelines to assist the replay officials.

The issue is particularly relevant because Belichick's North Carolina team lost to Syracuse on a controversial all-or-nothing two-point play in overtime. The ruling on the field was that Syracuse had successfully earned the decisive two points. The call was upheld via the available replay angles.

“If he scored he scored,” Belichick said Monday. “If he didn’t score, he didn’t score. Just put a camera there and get it right. That’s what I’m for. But based on what was called on the field, the views that the officials had, I don’t know how you could possibly overturn it. The view was from a long, long way away.”

At both the college and pro level, replay overturns the real-time ruling only if there is clear and obvious evidence to the contrary.

“From what the officials had to work with, it would be hard to tell,” Belichick said of the game-deciding play. “I think from what the fans showed — they had some good footage of it — that there are different views there that the officials in Charlotte, the headquarters there where they looked at reviews of the game, they didn't have those films. So the answer to the question is to put goal line and sideline cameras on the lines so that you have a good look at those plays.”

More official cameras would increase the chances of getting a decisive look.

"The ACC doesn't have goalline cameras," Belichick said. "They don't have sideline cameras, like the other conferences do, and that's something that I've always advocated when I was in the NFL for 20 years — sideline cameras, end zone cameras, like in tennis. Put on the sideline, put on the goal line, put on the end line. Those are the scoring [views], especially in college football, where you have the overtime rule, which is going to put you in the red zone. . . .

“All the other conferences have them. The ACC doesn't have them. I'm not sure why, but we've talked about that in league meetings. But for some reason, we don't have them, and I think it would be good for the game to get a definitive look at every play like that.”

He's right. Too much rides on these games to pinch pennies when it comes to the replay function. It's only as good as what the video evidence reveals. More video evidence is always better.

In the years since Belichick was fired by the Patriots, the NFL has implemented a Hawk-Eye system of stationary cameras in all stadiums that provides angles not provided by the TV broadcast, which has more or fewer cameras based on the window.

item.title: Jerry Jones: Troy Aikman working for Cowboys in future is "very possible"
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Troy Aikman was in Philadelphia to call Monday night's game between the Cowboys and the Eagles and he took some time before it got underway to catch up with his first boss in the NFL.
item.content:encoded:
Troy Aikman was in Philadelphia to call Monday night's game between the Cowboys and the Eagles and he took some time before it got underway to catch up with his first boss in the NFL.

Aikman's conversation with Cowboys owner Jerry Jones before the Dallas win comes at a moment of professional uncertainty for Aikman. His contract with ESPN will be up at the end of the season and he recently said he would "have a hard time not taking a good look" at a chance to work for the organization that drafted him with the first overall pick in 1989.

Aikman has worked as a consultant for the Dolphins and Jones was asked on 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday if he's open to the idea of Aikman taking on a significant role in the organization. Jones said he "could and would" be open to that notion and called Aikman "certainly qualified" to take on that kind of job.

"He’s one of the hardest working, most focused people that I’ve ever been around," Jones said. "When you’re around each other, a part of that makeup can make it where you have your ups and downs. I think the world of him. I’ve seen his image and had it in my eyes since I walked in the NFL. He's outstanding. The answer is not necessarily that we're going to do something more direct with the team at this time, but don’t rule it out. It is very possible."

Very possible and definitely happening are far from the same thing, but smoke signals about a possible partnership could prove to be foreshadowing for what will take place when and if it becomes definite that Aikman is going to be looking for a new job come the end of the 2026 season.

item.title: Mike Vrabel: Proud of Malik Willis for continuing to develop
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Mike Vrabel was Malik Willis’ head coach for the first two years of the quarterback’s career.
item.content:encoded:
Mike Vrabel was Malik Willis’ head coach for the first two years of the quarterback’s career.

A Titans third-round pick in 2022, Willis appeared in eight games with three starts under Vrabel as a rookie and then another three games in 2023.

The two will be on opposite sidelines on Sunday, as the Dolphins face the Patriots in South Florida.

Vrabel told reporters on Monday that working with Willis in Nashville was great.

“Malik’s continued to develop, and that’s the thing that I’m proud of him for, and I know that he should be proud of himself to continue to battle and go to Green Bay,” Vrabel said, via transcript from the team. “I try to stay in communication with him, tell him congrats and that I’m happy for him, and then he gets a deal in Miami.

“He’s very talented. He’s got a strong arm, can throw at different platforms. He’s a strong runner. I think he’s starting to see things a little quicker, a little clearer, just as he’s developed in the NFL.”

Through six games in 2026, Willis has completed 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,057 yards with four touchdowns and four interceptions. He’s also rushed for 223 yards with three TDs.

item.title: Colorado insider claims Deion Sanders has offered critics $50,000 to not talk about him
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As the fourth year of the Deion Sanders experiment in Colorado continues to collapse, a man with unique access to Coach Prime has made an eye-opening claim.
item.content:encoded:
As the fourth year of the Deion Sanders experiment in Colorado continues to collapse, a man with unique access to Coach Prime has made an eye-opening claim.

Christopher Neely, better known as "Uncle Neely," has served as Deion’s personal videographer. Via Essentially Sports, Neely recently said that Sanders has offered cash to his critics in an effort to get them to leave him alone.

"For the most part, the people that attack him wouldn't be making the money they were making if he wasn't here to attack," Neely said earlier this week. "Which is why he told some of them, 'Hey man, let's just do this. I give you $50,000 to not mention my name for a year.' And ain't nobody took the deal yet. . . . And you love talking about this man so much, and you make so much talking of this man that you turned the deal down."

Sanders has yet to confirm or deny Neely's contention. If true, it's stunning. And it's good to know that no one in the media has accepted the offer. It would violate any and all standards of journalism — if basic standards of journalism are still being widely practiced.

It also underscores the extreme level of sensitivity that Sanders has to criticism. Which, while not new for him, continues to be confounding.

How can so many people who have won at the game of life become so bothered by the basic scrutiny, and criticism, that comes with the territory? Nowadays, anyone and everyone with a public profile gets criticized somewhere. The only sensible approach is to ignore it. And, if for whatever reason the person being criticized is tormented by the possibility that they're not universally beloved, the best play is to not give oxygen to the critics by acknowledging it.

First, it only invites more criticism. Second, it makes the person who should otherwise ignore the criticism seem petty, small, and focused on all the wrong things.

Which, in Sanders's case, could help explain why the 2026 season continues to disintegrate. The only question left to answer at this point is whether he'll get a fifth year in Boulder or a buyout.

item.title: Sean McVay: Poor kickoff coverage is "one of those deals that’s driving me crazy"
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Rams have made several changes on special teams over the last couple of years, but the team’s results have still been poor — particularly on kick coverage.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams have made several changes on special teams over the last couple of years, but the team’s results have still been poor — particularly on kick coverage.

Despite getting a win over the Raiders on Sunday, the Rams allowed a 36-yard return on the game’s opening kickoff, then allowed another 42-yard return later in the first quarter.

After that, Los Angeles had Brandon McManus send the ball to the end zone for a touchback.

It’s a continuation of an issue the team has had all season. It’s partially the reason Blake Grupe suffered a torn ACL, as he had to make a tackle to prevent an even longer return on a kickoff in Week 6.

Head coach Sean McVay told reporters in his Monday news conference that the coverage issues were the same.

“It was not good enough,” McVay said, via transcript from the team. "We've talked about this a lot, and it has to get fixed. It's not good enough, and we cannot allow ourselves to do that. That was a great return unit that we were going against. [Raiders Special Teams Coordinator] Joe ‘D’ [DeCamillis] and those guys did a really good job, but we have to be much better. You can't give up the first two times that you cover that field position.”

So what can the Rams do going forward?

“I have to figure that out,” McVay said. “It's one of those deals that’s driving me crazy. We have to figure it out, and we haven't yet.”

The Rams have notoriously under-invested in special teams in recent years, and it has continued to affect games. It’s likely to cost the team again in 2026 — unless and until the team can finally effectively cover a kick.

item.title: John Harbaugh defends Cam Skattebo's helmet-lowering technique
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Sunday, Giants running back Cam Skattebo drew a rare flag for impermissible use of the helmet.
item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, Giants running back Cam Skattebo drew a rare flag for impermissible use of the helmet. On Monday, Giants coach John Harbaugh defended Skattebo's technique.

"I'm quite sure [Skattebo is] not trying to use his helmet as a weapon, as a battering ram," Harbaugh told reporters, via Jordan Raanan of ESPN. "It's not the way he's thinking. He's leading with his shoulder. That's what he's trying to do. . . . So, I didn't have a problem with the technique personally at all, but we haven't heard from the league. Maybe they'll be able to enlighten us a little bit on it in terms of what they want us to teach, and that would be great."

The language from the rulebook is as clear as it can be. Under Rule 12, Article 10(a), it's a foul if a player "lowers his head and makes forcible contact with his helmet against an opponent."

The NFL adopted that rule in 2018, as a proposal that was cobbled together, presented to ownership, and passed without any advance discussion or scrutiny from the media. Infractions are almost always fined after the fact. Skattebo's violation was flagged.

In Week 6 alone, the NFL imposed five fines for impermissible use of the helmet. In Week 5, six such fines were levied. For the year (including the preseason), 31 fines for impermissible use of the helmet have been imposed.

It's only an issue for coaches when it results in 15 yards of field position; the fines are paid by the players. If the league wants to truly get rid of the maneuver, flags need to fly. And then coaches will be incentivized to come up with a plan other than allowing players to use their helmets like a battering ram.

For now, Skattebo has vowed to keep doing it. If he does, the fines will increase. Eventually, he'll be looking at a suspension. And the officials will surely be watching him more closely for further violations — and possibly throwing more flags.

item.title: Cowboys regain lead on CeeDee Lamb's second TD
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The back-and-forth between the Cowboys and Eagles continues in the second half.
item.content:encoded:
The back-and-forth between the Cowboys and Eagles continues in the second half.

Only 4:14 after the Eagles took a 21-20 lead, the Cowboys regained it 28-21.

Dak Prescott threw a dart to CeeDee Lamb, who caught the ball in the end zone for a 16-yard touchdown. It was Lamb's second touchdown of the night. His first covered 9 yards.

Lamb has five catches for 74 yards.

The Cowboys drove 61 yards in nine plays, converting two third downs. That included a defensive holding penalty on Riq Woolen, who was covering Lamb, on a third-and-9. The 5-yard penalty, which came on an incompletion, extended the drive with an automatic first down.

Prescott has completed 14 of 25 passes for 206 yards and three touchdowns.

He ran in the 2-point conversion to make it a 7-point lead.

item.title: With games against the Bills and Jaguars looming, the Ravens need Lamar Jackson
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: There's no uncertainty as to whether the Ravens need quarterback Lamar Jackson.
item.content:encoded:
There's no uncertainty as to whether the Ravens need quarterback Lamar Jackson. There's plenty of uncertainty as to when he'll be able to play.

With him, they're 3-1. Without him, they're 1-2. With losses to the Browns and Bengals in the past eight days, the Ravens have started 0-2 in the AFC North for the first time since 2007.

Jackson made it clear on Friday that he's dealing with a high-ankle sprain, suffered in Week 4 against the Titans. He said at the time, as to the possibility of playing on Sunday against Cincinnati, “Right now, I’m heading in the right direction."

One day later, the Ravens downgraded Jackson from questionable to out.

With a Sunday trip to Buffalo coming, followed by a short-week visit from the Jaguars, Jackson's return becomes critical. Absent Jackson, Baltimore's 4-3 record could sink to 4-5 by next Friday.

So the question of the week in Baltimore becomes whether Jackson will play against Josh Allen and the Bills. As mentioned on Sunday's Football Night in America, it's unknown within the building whether he'll be able to return on Sunday — and any effort to predict when he'll be able to play is a guess.

Jackson made it clear during his Friday press conference that it's an issue of pain tolerance, and that the ankle sprain is keeping him from being as mobile as he needs to be. That's no surprise. A high-ankle sprain takes more time to heal than other types of sprains. He explained that he doesn't want to play if doing so would potentially hurt the team.

The challenge this week for the Ravens will be to get the eventual starter ready for the game. If Jackson is listed as a "full" participant on Wednesday, Thursday, and/or Friday, it will mean he has taken 100 percent of his normal first-team reps. Which also will mean that, if he doesn't play, backup Tyler Huntley won't be getting the first-team reps in preparation for Buffalo.

With or without Jackson, the next two games become critical to Baltimore's season. Win both, and they're right on track for reaching their goal. Lose both, and it could be another season without a ticket to the postseason party.

The chances of going 2-0, and not 0-2, will be much greater if Jackson is able to play. It's something that we'll find out as the current week unfolds.

item.title: Texans GM Nick Caserio: No knee-jerk reactions, significant personnel changes right now
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Texans had a chance to head into their bye week on a three-game winning streak, but they couldn't score any points to open overtime against the Giants and their run defense broke down as the visitors rolled to a game-winning touchdown by former Texan Devin Singletary.
item.content:encoded:
The Texans had a chance to head into their bye week on a three-game winning streak, but they couldn't score any points to open overtime against the Giants and their run defense broke down as the visitors rolled to a game-winning touchdown by former Texan Devin Singletary.

The loss dropped the Texans to 2-5, which is not where the team was projected to be given the preseason expectations in Houston and elsewhere. It does not sound like the disappointing start to the year is going to lead to any rash reactions from General Manager Nick Caserio.

At a press conference on Monday, Caserio said the team is "not going to make significant changes to personnel" before the offseason and that they aren't going to make "knee-jerk reactions" in the wake of their latest loss. Caserio said the solution is to "play more consistent football" than they've been able to play thus far.

“Some of our good players, our better players, probably haven’t played how they're capable of. That’s just the reality," Caserio said.

Caserio didn't name any names, but he highlighted penalties and tackling as areas where the Texans have been particularly poor through seven games. It's unclear how much those things will change in the middle of the season, but it's clear the Texans won't wind up where they want to go if they stay the same.

item.title: A 16-game international week was never a possibility during 2020 CBA talks
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Sunday, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers claimed that, during the 2020 Collective Bargaining Agreement negotiations, a discussion was had regarding the possibility of a full-blown "international week."
item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers claimed that, during the 2020 Collective Bargaining Agreement negotiations, a discussion was had regarding the possibility of a full-blown "international week." With all 32 teams playing in foreign countries on the same weekend.

It sounded odd, and impractical. As best we can tell, it was never a serious consideration during the 2020 CBA talks — if it was even a consideration at all.

While it's possible that the league chose 17 regular-season games over the ability to stage up to 16 annual international games, there was never a specific plan to play all 16 international games in the same week.

It's borderline ludicrous on its face. No games in any U.S. stadiums? Sixteen games played all over the world? With a Thursday night game, 14 on Sunday, and one on Monday night? It would be a logistical nightmare for the NFL, which would be staging a full slate of games in foreign soil in the same four-day window.

The goal was, and still is, to turn the European games into a TV package, with multiple games starting at 9:30 a.m. ET. Emptying the international tank on one and only one weekend would make no sense.

And there's no way the NFL would have accepted 16 international games plus two byes. The league experimented with two byes in 1993, and the networks hated it. A second bye extends the season, but it dilutes the number of games played in plenty of weeks with byes.

In 1993, eight of 28 teams were off in Week 3, Week 4, Week 6, and Week 8. Six teams were off in Week 6, Week 11, and Week 13. Four teams were off in Week 10. And two teams were off in Week 12.

While two byes may be needed to sell an 18-game season to the players, the league wouldn't have added a second bye to a 16-game season. (Indeed, it didn't add a second bye to a 17-game season.)

More importantly, and despite Rodgers's claim, a full-league international week never was (and never will be) a realistic possibility.

item.title: Jesse Minter: Lamar Jackson is "working his butt off to be back"
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Baltimore's HC told reporters on Monday he thinks Jackson will be "in a decent spot" to return for Sunday's game against the Bills.
item.content:encoded:
As the Ravens turn the page to their Week 8 matchup against the Bills, it's unclear whether or not their starting quarterback will be back.

Lamar Jackson appeared to be on track to play in yesterday's game against the Bengals until he wasn't, with the team downgrading him to out on Saturday — even though the Ravens were playing at home.

Will he return from his high-ankle sprain against the Bills?

"Yeah, I think, again, Lamar is working his butt off to be back and be out there," head coach Jesse Minter said in his Monday press conference. "I think he was able to get in a little bit of work, obviously, toward the end of last week.

"So, I think he’ll be in a decent spot. But we’ll know a lot more on Wednesday."

While there was some reporting that the Ravens were “shocked” when Jackson was not ready to play on Saturday, Minter said that was “a little bit” of a mischaracterization of the situation.

“But, again, we kind of had Saturday that we would… got a little bit of work in on Friday, come in Saturday and feel it out and see where it’s at and see how it’s going, how it’s feeling, how it responded,” Minter said. "And then what happened, happened.

“I’m not going to speak, really, on the details of anybody’s injury,” Minter added. “So, look, if he’s able to play — that’s healthy enough to play, and play the way that obviously we feel like he needs to play — then he will play.”

With Baltimore blowing double-digit leads to divisional opponents in each of the last two weeks, the club could certainly use the boost from a healthy Jackson returning.

After three limited practices last week, we’ll see if Jackson is on the field and able to participate in full starting with Wednesday’s injury report.

item.title: Klint Kubiak: Kirk Cousins is our starting quarterback
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Kubiak added that there's "no controversy" at the position.
item.content:encoded:
There won't be a quarterback change in Las Vegas this week.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak opened his Monday press conference by saying that Kirk Cousins will be the team's starter for their Week 8 game against the Jets. The announcement came a day after Kubiak said the team is "thinking about everything to fix our problems" when asked about turning to rookie Fernando Mendoza.

"There is no controversy there," Kubiak said. "He's playing at a very high level. He's gotta continue to do that for us to win and we gotta keep helping all the areas around him. Excited for him to go play against the Jets."

Kubiak said that Mendoza is "going to play at some point," but reiterated that Cousins is playing well and that the Raiders are "in the hunt" with a 3-4 record on the season.

Cousins was 26-of-44 for 295 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams, but did much of his damage after the Raiders fell behind 28-3 in the first half of the game.

item.title: Monday Night Football: Cowboys run past Eagles 38-21
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Javonte Williams had a career-high 155 yards, and Dak Prescott threw three touchdowns.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys saved their season, at least for another week, and the Eagles' postseason hopes took a huge hit Monday night. Dallas beat Philadelphia 38-21 to end a two-game losing streak and move to 3-4.

The Eagles, who are decimated by injuries, have lost five in a row to fall to 2-5. They started the game without quarterback Jalen Hurts and wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, among others, and finished it without running backs Saquon Barkley and Dameon Pierce.

Barkley, who was returning after missing two games with a hamstring injury, left with a back injury. He had seven carries for 62 yards and a touchdown and two catches for 9 yards in limited usage before his new injury. Pierce left in the fourth quarter with an undisclosed injury after 14 carries for 47 yards and a touchdown.

The game was back-and-forth for most of the night, with six lead changes. The last came on CeeDee Lamb's 16-yard touchdown reception and Dak Prescott's 2-point conversion that gave the Cowboys a 28-21 lead with 1:30 left in the third quarter.

Brian Schottenheimer, whose play calling was criticized after he abandoned the run in the second half last week, called for more runs than passes. The Cowboys ran it 38 times for 204 yards and threw it 27 times for 212 yards. The Eagles had zero tackles for loss.

Javonte Williams set a career-high with 155 yards and scored a touchdown on 25 carries. He is the Cowboys' first 150-yard rusher since Ezekiel Elliott in 2018.

Prescott was 15-of-27 for 212 yards and three touchdowns. Lamb caught five passes for 74 yards and two touchdowns and George Pickens had four receptions for 57 yards and a touchdown.

Tanner McKee, starting for the second consecutive week in place of Hurts, went 23-of-35 for 211 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown picked him in the second half.

Rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon caught seven passes for 67 yards and a touchdown.

item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Eagles running back entered with a right hamstring injury.
item.content:encoded:
Saquon Barkley missed two games with a right hamstring injury. He returned tonight, but the Eagles running back was in obvious pain for much of the night.

He is now questionable to return with a back injury.

It is his third injury of the season, with a stinger earlier this season.

Barkley has seven carries for 62 yards and a touchdown and two catches for 9 yards. He has played 10 snaps.

The Eagles are in trouble without him, now down 10 points to the Cowboys. Dallas drove 78 yards in nine plays to the Philadelphia 6 before settling for Brandon Aubrey's 24-yard field goal.

item.title: PFT's Week 8 NFL 2026 power rankings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: There's a new no. 1, by default.
item.content:encoded:
1. Bills (last week No. 3; 5-1): For the first time ever, a team ascends to No. 1 without playing.

2. Jaguars (No. 4; 4-2): For the first time ever, a team ascends to No. 2 without playing.

3. Vikings (No. 5; 6-0): A four-game gauntlet is coming.

4. 49ers (No. 1; 6-1): The bye week came at the best possible time.

5. Chiefs (No. 2; 5-1): They badly need help at receiver.

6. Broncos (No. 6; 5-2): Take that, Ryan Fitzpatrick.

7. Seahawks (No. 7; 4-3): Can they do to Caleb Williams what they did to Patrick Mahomes?

8. Bears (No. 10; 5-2): The NFC Championship matchup we almost got in January happens on Monday night.

9. Browns (No. 11; 5-2): If they can complete the sweep of the Steelers, they'll control the division.

10. Steelers (No. 13; 5-2): Sunday's home game against Cleveland is the closest thing to a "must" win that any 5-2 team will ever have.

11. Patriots (No. 8; 4-3): With the Packers and Lions looming, they can't overlook the Dolphins.

12. Bengals (No. 14; 4-2): Ja'Marr Chase's halftime speech may have saved the season.

13. Lions (No. 18; 4-2): Can Jared Goff figure out the Brian Flores defense?

14. Packers (No. 9; 4-3): They can't let one loss become two on Thursday night.

15. Ravens (No. 12; 4-3): It feels like the entire season hinges on the next two games (at Bills, Jaguars).

16. Rams (No. 17; 3-4): If they can keep running the ball the way they did on Sunday, they can start stacking wins.

17. Giants (No. 21; 4-2-1): They're becoming the most fun team to watch in the entire league.

18. Falcons (No. 24; 3-4): More Jekyll, less Hyde.

19. Raiders (No. 16; 3-4): Mendoza time is coming.

20. Buccaneers (No. 29; 2-5): The NFC South is still theirs for the taking.

21. Cowboys (No. 23; 3-4): The best solution for a bad defense is an offense that stays on the field for as long as it can.

22. Panthers (No. 15; 3-3): Drinks are on the house.

23. Texans (No. 19; 2-5): Has an elite defense ever fallen apart this quickly?

24. Saints (No. 20; 2-5): The win over the Giants may have saved Kellen Moore from a bye-week buh-bye.

25. Cardinals (No. 22; 2-5): It's Carson Beck time.

26. Eagles (No. 25; 2-5): Lose to the 1-4-1 Commanders on Sunday night, and this season is over. (It may be anyway.)

27. Titans (No. 26; 1-6): Will they ever win two in a row again?

28. Colts (No. 27; 2-5): The trade deadline could get very interesting.

29. Dolphins (No. 31; 1-5): Only five weeks until the next Jets game.

30. Commanders (No. 30; 1-4-1): Did Dan Quinn know it was the bye week?

31. Jets (No. 28; 2-5): The clock is ticking on Aaron Glenn.

32. Chargers (No. 32; 0-6): "Last winless team in the league" wasn't mentioned in their schedule-release video.

item.title: Aaron Glenn: Garrett Wilson sideline conversation "overblown," we want to get him the ball
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson was seen in an animated conversation with quarterback Geno Smith and assistant coaches on the bench during Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins, but it's not an issue for head coach Aaron Glenn.
item.content:encoded:
Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson was seen in an animated conversation with quarterback Geno Smith and assistant coaches on the bench during Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins, but it's not an issue for head coach Aaron Glenn.

Wilson said after the game that the conversation was "heated," but not because of anger toward one another. Wilson said he was "disappointed with how we was playing up to that point and wanted to be more aggressive" when the team had the ball and Glenn said on Monday that he thought everyone involved was coming from the right place.

"I think sometimes that's overblown as far as what people think is happening," Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "Sometimes those conversations can be totally something else. I know for a fact that Geno, Garrett, it was more or less, 'Let's get going. Let's get the offense going,' more than guys bickering at each other. I think sometimes that gets overblown. I know what type of player Garrett is, and I know what type of player Geno is. I know where their hearts at, too. I know for a fact that was more or less let's get the offense going and try to score points."

Wilson had two catches for 26 yards on three targets against Miami and he's had nine catches in the team's last three losses, which has sparked discussion about whether the team is doing enough to get their top wideout the ball. Glenn said the Jets are "trying to get the ball to Garrett as much as we can" while also making smart choices in the flow of each game.

"You take a look at that situation and obviously in this game they were trying to make sure they take Garrett out, but to be honest with you, that wasn't the issue when it comes to our offense," Glenn said. "I thought we moved the ball, I thought we scored points, but we know for a fact that every game, man, Garrett is our top priority to make sure we get the ball."

Sunday's game featured a season-high in yards and points for the Jets, but neither were enough to beat a winless Dolphins team and things are likely to remain heated around the team until they wind up in the win column more often.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Eagles added three players to their active roster ahead of Monday night's game against the Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles added three players to their active roster ahead of Monday night's game against the Cowboys.

Guard Landon Dickerson was activated from injured reserve along with tight ends Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers. Cornerback Jakorian Bennett has also been designated for return, but remains on injured reserve.

Dickerson started the opener at left guard, but has been out with a knee injury for the last five games. Calcaterra has been out the whole year with a back injury and Stowers has missed all six games with a quad injury. Stowers was a second-round pick this year, so Monday is set to be his NFL debut.

The Eagles also elevated running back Elijah Mitchell and linebacker Keyshawn James-Newby from the practice squad on a temporary basis.

item.title: Saquon Barkley addressed teammates after loss: "Never quit, never give up"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Eagles fell to 2-5 on Monday night, but Barkley doesn't want to see anyone quitting on the season.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said after Monday night's loss to the Cowboys that he had addressed his teammates to tell them how important it is that they keep competing, even as they struggle through a five-game losing streak.

The 2-5 Eagles are long shots to make the playoffs, but Barkley reminded teammates that they can still turn the season around.

"I'm not really a big talker, to be honest," Barkley told reporters. "Felt like the moment was right. I just, how I look at life, I feel like you just never quit. You never give up. You just keep fighting, no matter what, whatever the situation is, how it looks. And I feel like that we have the men in the locker room to do it. We put ourselves in this situation. We've got to get ourselves out of it. I know that I've got to take more of a a role of being vocal, using my voice. I'm more of a lead-by-example type of guy, but it happens when you have guys banged up."

Barkley said quarterback Jalen Hurts is ordinarily the team's vocal leader. Hurts is out for the season because of blood clots, and Barkley said he and some of his veteran teammates have to take it upon themselves to fill that void.

"I think we're doing a great job leading, and we're working our ass off," Barkley said. "And it sucks when the results aren't going the way you wanted to go. I'm going to sound a broken record, but I really bought into this mindset. Just got to keep believing in the process, keep working and keep going. The results may not be what we want right now, but it doesn't matter. We've got to go back to work. It takes all of us."

Barkley came into the game with a hamstring injury, aggravated it on his first run, and hurt his back while trying to play while compensating for the lack of mobility in his hamstring. But he said he's not thinking about shutting things down to preserve his health.

"It sucks when it's not going the way you want it to go," Barkley said. "I truly love this game and I feel like if you're able to go, you've got to push your body to the limit."

item.content:encoded:
Ravens rookie guard Vega Ioane had to leave Sunday's loss to the Bengals with a knee injury and a report on Tuesday suggests he'll miss some more time before returning to action.

NFL Media reports that Ioane has been diagnosed with an MCL sprain. The injury is expected to have him out of the lineup in the near future.

Ioane opened the season at right guard and moved to center after injuries to Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic. The Ravens traded for Cam Jurgens and he made his debut against Cincinnati, which had Ioane back on the right side before his injury.

Andrew Vorhees was inactive in Week 7, so Emory Jones replaced Ioane against the Bengals. The Ravens will likely have to turn to one of those players against the Bills in Week 8.

item.title: Landon Dickerson feels he let team down in his return to lineup
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Eagles got left guard Landon Dickerson back in the lineup for Monday night's game against the Cowboys, but his return wasn't enough to snap the team's losing streak.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles got left guard Landon Dickerson back in the lineup for Monday night's game against the Cowboys, but his return wasn't enough to snap the team's losing streak.

That streak reached five games as the Cowboys outscored the home team 28-7 over the final 43 minutes of the game. The Eagles' last real chance came when they got the ball down 10 with just over six minutes to play, but pass protection broke down on their first two snaps with Cowboys defensive tackle Quinnen Williams getting a sack on the second one. The Eagles wound up turning it over on downs and the Cowboys put the finishing touches on a 38-21 win.

Dickerson got beat on the Williams sack and he was hard on himself while speaking to reporters after the game. Dickerson said that the "two plays at the end there f—king lose us the game” and he said that it hurt to feel you "let your guys down."

"I didn’t play good enough," Dickerson said, via NBCSportsPhiladelphia.com. "These guys work their ass off to come in here and compete every day. I wasn’t good enough."

Dickerson said he felt fine in his return from a knee injury and the Eagles ran behind him with success early in the game, but Saquon Barkley had to leave with an injury and the run game became less of an option once Dallas moved in front on the scoreboard. That had more to do with defensive breakdowns than anything Dickerson was doing, but that didn't impact his negative assessment of his play in his first game back.

item.title: Javonte Williams: Good to give confidence to keep calling runs
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Given the number of factors that go into determining winners and losers in NFL games, it's hard to pin the Cowboys' back-to-back losses solely on running back Javonte Williams carrying the ball 23 times in Weeks 5 and 6.
item.content:encoded:
Given the number of factors that go into determining winners and losers in NFL games, it's hard to pin the Cowboys' back-to-back losses solely on running back Javonte Williams carrying the ball 23 times in Weeks 5 and 6.

Offensive balance is always a good thing, though, and it wasn't hard to notice a difference in how the Cowboys were attacking the Eagles on Monday night. Williams kept getting the ball and it didn't feel like a coincidence that they fed an effort that resulted in a convincing 38-21 road win.

Williams ran 25 times for a career-high 155 yards and sealed the win with a fourth quarter touchdown. The Cowboys also gave the ball to Tyler Goodson 11 times while Dak Prescott was connecting with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens for three touchdowns through the air.

"It was good to give [head coach Brian Schottenheimer] the confidence to keep calling the runs," Williams said, via the team's website. "He made a big emphasis on that this week — to get at least 25 rushes in a game. . . . We were just trying to get back to a balanced offense, and I feel like we did a great job tonight. We've got a high-powered offense, and when you've got G.P., CeeDee, Jake Ferguson, those guys on the outside, I mean, it's going to open up the running."

The Cowboys only managed 29 points in their losses to the Packers and Buccaneers in the previous two games and that's not a recipe for success for a team that's built around an ability to score points in bunches. Monday night was more like it and the Cowboys will be trying to stay in the groove they found in Philadelphia.

item.title: Cowboys are the betting favorites to win the NFC East after win in Philadelphia
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Cowboys are not in first place in the NFC East, but they will be at the end of the season, if the betting odds are to be believed.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys are not in first place in the NFC East, but they will be at the end of the season, if the betting odds are to be believed.

After Monday night's win in Philadelphia, Dallas is a +115 favorite to win the NFC East. Just behind the Cowboys are the Giants at +125. The Commanders are long shots at +800 and the Eagles are the longest shots at +1500.

Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said after the game that the importance of winning on the road in the division wasn't lost on him.

"I think it gets us right back into the hunt in the NFC East," Schottenheimer said.

The 4-2-1 Giants have a 1.5-game lead over the 3-4 Cowboys, and the Giants beat the Cowboys in Week 1, so it might seem like the Giants should be favored. But the perception among bettors is that the Cowboys remain the better team, as they were expected to be before the season.

The Giants-Cowboys rematch is Week 17 in Dallas. The NFC East may be on the line when the two teams meet again.

item.title: Oregon QB Dante Moore won't return this season from his concussion
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore, who entered the season as one of the top prospects in the 2027 draft, will not play again during the 2026 season.
item.content:encoded:
Oregon quarterback Dante Moore, who entered the season as one of the top prospects in the 2027 draft, will not play again during the 2026 season.

Coach Dan Lanning announced on Monday that Moore's concussion from last month will sideline him for the balance of the schedule.

"If it was up to Dante in any shape, way, he would be out there playing for the guys," Lanning said. "This isn't a selfish decision on Dante's part, saying, 'I don't want to come back, the season doesn't look the way I want it to look.' That's not at all what this is."

Lanning said that Moore has not been cleared to return from the concussion suffered on September 26 against USC. After taking an illegal hit while sliding, Moore was taken to a local hospital by ambulance for evaluation.

"We said before that this is a serious deal that he'll 100% be able to fully recover from, that hasn't changed," Lanning said. "But for him to be out there on the field for us, that's not going to happen. We'd love to have Dante out there, he's still going to be a big part of this team."

The Ducks entered the season ranked No. 2. They're now 4-3 and out of the top 25.

Under the NCAA's new five-year rule, Moore can return to college football in 2027, delaying his entry to the draft until 2028.

item.title: Dez Bryant wants a full investigation following a Sunday citation for assault
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Former Cowboys receiver Dez Bryant wants a full investigation following an incident that resulted in the three-time Pro Bowler being cited for assault.
item.content:encoded:
Former Cowboys receiver Dez Bryant wants a full investigation following an incident that resulted in the three-time Pro Bowler being cited for assault.

Bryant shared his version of the situation with Jackson Thompson of Outkick. Bryant claims that a police officer aimed a gun at Bryant in front of his daughters Sunday following a confrontation with a man that Bryant contends threatened to shoot him.

He accused a pair of drivers of cutting him off, and it went from there between Bryant and one of the men.

"He go to threatening me and basically saying, um, he’ll insinuate that he’ll, you know, he’ll shoot me or whatever," Bryant told Thompson. Replied Bryant, "You pull that gun, I’m telling you right now, you better use it because if you don’t I’m going to do something to you."

The man was recording Bryant with his phone. Bryant told Thompson that he knocked the phone out of the man's hand. The man then threatened to call police; Bryant encouraged him to do it.

A responding officer drew a gun on Bryant. Bryant's girlfriend arrived at the scene with Bryant's daughters and began recording the interaction.

The man, 19-year-old Noah Reyes, gave his version to the California Post on Monday. Reyes also shared the footage he recorded.

"Several callers reported that multiple individuals were involved in the altercation as well as a possible weapon," a Southlake (Texas) Police Department spokesperson told the Post in a statement. "Based on that information, officers drew their firearms upon arrival as a precaution to address any potential threats and ensure the safety of everyone at the scene. Several individuals were temporarily detained as part of the investigation. No firearms were recovered at the scene.

"The altercation reportedly began as a traffic incident near Kimball Avenue, where one of the involved individuals, identified as 37-year-old Desmond Bryant, reported he was cut off by another motorist. Both parties subsequently entered the parking lot, where an argument ensued and the alleged assault occurred.

"Following the investigation, Bryant, was issued a citation for Assault by Contact, a Class C misdemeanor, and was released at the scene."

Bryant is due in court on November 20. Reyes plans to sue Bryant for an injury to his hand.

A first-round pick in 2010, Bryant spent eight seasons with the Cowboys. He played for the Saints in 2018 and the Ravens in 2020.

item.title: NFL fines Caleb Williams $11,941 for displaying "unauthorized logo" on his shoes in Week 6
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The No Fun League is also the No Footwear League.
item.content:encoded:
The No Fun League is also the No Footwear League. More specifically, no footwear made by companies that don't pay the league.

Per a source with knowledge of the situation, the league has fined Bears quarterback Caleb Williams $11,941 for displaying an "unauthorized logo" on his shoes during the Week 6 win over the Falcons in Atlanta.

Williams was wearing Caddix cleats, which do not have a deal with the NFL for the use of its shoes in NFL games.

Williams has appealed the fine, and his argument will be, we're told, that he believes the shoes are safer than the shoe options that are officially licensed by the NFL.

He has worn the same type of shoe throughout the 2026 preseason and during all regular-season games in which he has played. He was not fined for Week 1 and Week 2. He has yet to be fined for the Week 7 Thursday night game against the Patriots.

It's his intention, we're also told, to continue wearing the shoes.

The fine letter, dated October 20, does not mention the possibility of Williams being prevented from playing with the Caddix logo visible on his shoes.

It's an interesting situation for the league. If a player subjectively believes that a given shoe that isn't made by a company that pays the NFL for the privilege of displaying its logo is safer, should the player be prevented from wearing it?

Then there's the separate question of whether objective data supports that the shoe is safer. If that's the case, it will be another example of the commitment to health and safety yielding on occasion to dollars and cents.

The Bears return to action next Monday night against the Seahawks. And it will make plenty of sense to eyeball the items that Williams has on his feet.

item.title: Eagles take 21-20 lead on Cowboys to open second half
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Rookie Makai Lemon scored his first NFL touchdown, a 4-yard reception from Tanner McKee.
item.content:encoded:
Rookie Makai Lemon scored his first NFL touchdown, a 4-yard reception from Tanner McKee. That put the Eagles back in front of the Cowboys, 21-20, after Jake Elliott's PAT.

The Eagles took the second-half kickoff and went 84 yards in 17 plays, taking 9:16 off the clock.

They converted 4-of-5 third downs and had a fourth-down conversion on the one third down they didn't convert.

The Eagles now have 238 yards.

McKee is 14-of-22 for 129 yards and a touchdown, and Lemon has five receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown.

Saquon Barkley has touched the ball on every play he's been on the field, with seven carries for 62 yards and two catches for 9 yards.

item.title: NFL announces Jay-Z as the Super Bowl LXI halftime act
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As expected, the selection of Super Bowl halftime show producer Jay-Z to perform at halftime of Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium is . . .
item.content:encoded:
As expected, the selection of Super Bowl halftime show producer Jay-Z to perform at halftime of Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium is . . . Jay-Z.

The NFL made the announcement at halftime of Monday night's Cowboys-Eagles game.

“For several years, we’ve had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I’ve seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show,” NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. “When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him. I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage.”

The partnership between Roc Nation and the NFL to produce the Super Bowl halftime show was struck in 2019.

Given the audience that the Super Bowl attracts, the halftime show has become the biggest annual stage in all of music.

item.title: Monday Night Football: Cowboys lead Eagles 20-14 at halftime
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Cowboys gained 275 yards, scoring on four of five possessions.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys and Eagles played an entertaining first half, combining for 34 points and 429 yards. The teams scored six times in nine possessions, and the Cowboys lead 20-14 at halftime.

The Cowboys scored on four of five possessions, getting a 55-yard field goal from Brandon Aubrey, a 9-yard CeeDee Lamb touchdown reception, a 21-yard George Pickens touchdown reception and a 27-yard Aubrey field goal.

Aubrey's chip-shot field goal came on the final play of the half, but on third down as the Cowboys left the field with a timeout in their pocket. Poor clock management cost them a chance at another play from the Philadelphia 9-yard line.

The Cowboys outgained the Eagles 275 to 154, with 18 runs and 21 passes. Dak Prescott is 12-of-21 for 174 yards and two touchdowns, and Javonte Williams has 10 carries for 67 yards.

Lamb has four catches for 58 yards and a touchdown and Pickens has caught three passes for 51 yards and a touchdown.

The Eagles scored on their first two drives, going 75 yards in only four plays and 76 yards in 13 plays. They have gotten plenty of help from the Dallas defense, which has five penalties. Four of those resulted in first downs, and three came on third- or fourth-down stops.

Saquon Barkley, who missed the past two games with a hamstring injury, has six carries for 50 yards and a touchdown. His first carry went for 29 yards and his second was an 8-yard touchdown run.

Barkley also has two catches for 9 yards.

Dameon Pierce has seven carries for 36 yards and a touchdown.

Tanner McKee is 7-of-13 for 68 yards.

item.title: George Pickens' highlight-reel TD catch puts Cowboys back on top
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Brian Schottenheimer said he wanted to see more out of wide receiver George Pickens this week.
item.content:encoded:
Brian Schottenheimer said he wanted to see more out of wide receiver George Pickens this week. Pickens gave him a highlight-reel touchdown catch.

On third-and-3 from the Philadelphia 21, Dak Prescott threw a dot to the back corner of the end zone. Pickens, who was tightly covered by safety Andrew Mukuba, made a spectacular catch and managed to get both feet in bounds.

It was Pickens' second catch of the night on three targets, and he has 30 yards.

The Cowboys lead 17-14 as neither defense has a stop yet.

The Cowboys have outgained the Eagles 191 to 140, with one extra possession.

Prescott is 8-of-13 for 96 yards and two touchdowns.
